concepts.name: configuration
concepts.description: The process of arranging components or parameters to meet a set of constraints and goals by selecting and sizing parts, ensuring compatibility, and validating against requirements.

concepts.name: constraint satisfaction
concepts.description: A process in which a solution must meet all specified constraints (e.g. cost limits, size and material requirements, etc.).

concepts.name: constraint type
concepts.description: The category of a requirement, such as dimensional, cost, mass, or material constraint.

concepts.name: hierarchical configuration
concepts.description: Organising configuration tasks from high (system)-level down to detailed low-level component specifications.

concepts.name: causal reasoning
concepts.description: Understanding the effect of changing one parameter on the other parts of the configuration.

concepts.name: teleological reasoning
concepts.description: Designing with the end goal in mind, ensuring that each decision contributes to the intended purpose of the system.

concepts.name: basement
concepts.description: The lowest storey/level of a building, wholly or partially underground. A structure with defined length, width, and height, subdivided into rooms that must meet area and dimension constraints.

concepts.name: chair
concepts.description: A piece of furniture composed of parts such as legs, seat, arms, and back, each with material, size, mass, and cost attributes.

concepts.name: material
concepts.description: The substance from which a component is made, affecting cost, mass, and durability.

concepts.name: component
concepts.description: A part of a larger configuration, such as a room in a basement or a leg in a chair.
